instructions: Return a short direct answer first. Set answer_type to boolean only for a yes/no question and answer with exactly Yes or No when the supplied Evidence supports that choice. Use answer_type=unanswerable when the supplied Evidence is insufficient or ambiguous and use a concise abstention answer; the runtime normalizes it to Unanswerable. Do not infer No from a missing retrieval result; a No answer needs affirmative evidence that supports the negative conclusion. For a what/which question asking for entities such as languages, methods, datasets, or values, return the entities explicitly stated in the Evidence even when only one is stated. Do not require proof that the list is exhaustive unless the question explicitly asks for all, every, or a complete list. Resolve words such as other relative to the question's stated reference point; do not treat other as a demand for multiple entities. Never invent additional list members. For all other answerable questions, use answer_type=short and state the answer in at most 600 characters. Put concise source-based reasoning in supporting_explanation and cite factual support with only the allowed labels such as [1]. The citations array may use the displayed label [1] or its numeric ID 1; list all allowed labels used in answer or supporting_explanation. Do not include a citation you cannot see in the supplied Evidence. Do not use external knowledge, guess, or claim that the paper omits a topic merely because no matching passage was retrieved. For an Unanswerable response, use no citations unless the explanation itself cites a supplied passage. Do not include markdown or extra keys.
